title: Microsoft Targets Rogue AI Agents With Dynamic Permissions, Risk Scoring
content_md: Microsoft on Monday announced new controls to monitor and restrict potentially rogue AI agents in enterprise environments, arguing that organizations should treat these agents as insiders rather than trusted software. The capabilities extend Project Perception , the agentic security system Microsoft launched in July. Perception was initially pitched as a defense against AI-driven attacks from outside, but it is now being applied to the agents companies run internally. Hayete Gallot, executive vice president of Microsoft Security, said companies tend to trust the agents they deploy by default. She warned that frontier models are trained to get results and aren’t built around organizational norms or judgment. “These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes,” Gallot wrote. Nadim Abdo, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of identity and network access, clarified the insider label. “This does not mean agents are inherently malicious. It means they are capable tools that can be granted access to important systems by users. They can make mistakes, be manipulated, or be compromised,” he explained. One of the new features, Dynamic Permissions, gives agents no permissions, or the bare minimum, at the outset.
